story: As an Aurora Storefront shopper, I want my account to lock after too many wrong passwords, so that nobody can guess their way into it. The lock should last a while and the sign-in page should tell me what happened.

story_analysis.invest_overall: A testable story once the lock duration is written down.

vague_phrases.suggestion: Nobody can test 'too many' - give the number of attempts.
A duration nobody wrote down becomes a guess in the code.

missing_elements: What support can do to unlock an account early
suggested_rewrites: As an Aurora Storefront shopper, I want my account locked for 30 minutes after 5 failed sign-in attempts within 10 minutes, so that nobody can guess their way in.
generated_acceptance_criteria: The account locks after 5 failed sign-in attempts within 10 minutes
A locked account stays locked for 30 minutes
The sign-in page tells the shopper the lock lasts 30 minutes
A successful sign-in resets the failed attempt counter to zero
risks: A shared lockout counter is needed once more than one server is live

forks.topic: Does the 10 minute window slide or reset?
Is the lock message shown before or after the fifth attempt?

criteria: The account locks after 5 failed sign-in attempts within 10 minutes
A locked account stays locked for 30 minutes
The sign-in page tells the shopper the lock lasts 30 minutes
A successful sign-in resets the failed attempt counter to zero

failure_modes.title: Two web servers count failed attempts separately
failure_modes.effect: An attacker keeps guessing past the fifth attempt, so the lock never protects the account
failure_modes.cause: Each web server counts failed attempts in its own memory instead of one shared store
failure_modes.severity_reason: The account can be taken over although the lock looks like it works
failure_modes.likelihood_reason: Aurora Storefront already runs more than one web server behind a load balancer
failure_modes.detectability_reason: A one-server test environment never shows it
failure_modes.test_idea: Send the five failed sign-ins through two different servers and check the account still locks

failure_modes.title: The 10 minute window is measured from the first attempt, not the last
failure_modes.effect: A patient attacker never trips the lock
failure_modes.cause: The window resets on a timer instead of sliding with each attempt
failure_modes.severity_reason: The lock can be walked around, but only slowly
failure_modes.likelihood_reason: The story does not say which window the team should build
failure_modes.test_idea: Fail four times, wait nine minutes, fail twice more

failure_modes.title: The lock message tells an attacker the account exists
failure_modes.cause: The message is only shown for accounts that really exist
failure_modes.severity_reason: No account is taken over by itself
failure_modes.likelihood_reason: The wording is already generic elsewhere on the site
failure_modes.test_idea: Trigger the lock on a real and an unknown email and compare the messages
